status: measured and recorded. A remainder this repository published one round earlier is WITHDRAWN as wrong, and replaced by the measurement that refutes it. A second, different gap in the same instrument is identified and is real. No published number changes.
subject: src/aionq/mode_locality.py, and the nearest-neighbour condition in src/aionq/matchgate.py::matchgate_plan

withdrawn_claim.what_it_said: matchgate_plan certifies nearest-neighbour adjacency in the qubit ordering, which is a ONE-DIMENSIONAL condition. The classical reason free-fermion counting is tractable -- Kasteleyn orientations and the FKT algorithm -- requires PLANARITY, which Euler's formula supplies and which is strictly weaker than 1D adjacency. So there are plausibly free-fermion circuits on planar but non-linear layouts that matchgate_plan refuses.
withdrawn_claim.why_it_is_wrong: it reasoned about the gate LAYOUT while the constraint lives in the ENCODING. Under Jordan-Wigner the modes of qubit k carry a string of Z operators from every qubit below it, so a two-qubit gate spanning a gap acquires the string of the qubits it jumps and the resulting operator is not quadratic in Majoranas. A matchgate matrix on non-adjacent qubits is not a free-fermion operation at all.
withdrawn_claim.how_it_was_caught: by measuring it instead of leaving it as a remainder, on instruction not to take a proposal at face value. The remainder was written in the same round that introduced the covariant defect capable of settling it, and was not settled with it.

measurement_1_adjacency_is_semantic.instrument: aionq.majorana.gaussian_defect, which is exactly O(2n)-invariant, on the full unitary of a 3-qubit circuit containing one gate
measurement_1_adjacency_is_semantic.the_sharp_form: the SAME matrix is free-fermion on adjacent qubits and not free-fermion one qubit further apart. Nothing about the gate changed; the Jordan-Wigner string of the qubit it jumped did. Certification and Gaussianity agree on every placement in the register, not only on the chosen one.
measurement_1_adjacency_is_semantic.consequence: matchgate_plan is not imposing a relaxable layout convention. It is enforcing the encoding, and its locality condition is correct rather than conservative.

measurement_2_the_real_gap_is_arity.result: a 3-qubit unitary built from a quadratic Majorana generator has gaussian_defect 2.8e-15 and is refused by matchgate_plan with 'acts on 3 qubits; free-fermion evolution is generated by quadratic terms only'
measurement_2_the_real_gap_is_arity.reading: the certificate is SEMANTIC in its locality condition and SYNTACTIC in its arity condition: it recognises presentations, not operations. A poly-time-simulable unitary is priced as hard purely for how it was written down.
measurement_2_the_real_gap_is_arity.direction_of_the_error: the refusal raises the reported bound, which is the safe direction for an upper bound and the wrong direction for a measurement. No published number is affected, because no corpus circuit is presented this way.
measurement_2_the_real_gap_is_arity.not_repaired: accepting multi-qubit gates would require deciding Gaussianity of an arbitrary 2^k x 2^k unitary inside the certified path, which is a change to a bound-feeding instrument and is not this round's to make. Recorded, not fixed.

measurement_3_what_adjacency_costs.counting: a quadratic generator c_j c_k is directly expressible as a same-or-adjacent-qubit gate exactly when |j//2 - k//2| <= 1: n same-qubit pairs plus 4(n-1) adjacent-qubit pairs
measurement_3_what_adjacency_costs.closed_form: reachable(n) = 5n - 4, verified against the explicit count for n = 2..19
measurement_3_what_adjacency_costs.but_it_is_generating: the 11 reachable generators at n = 3 Lie-generate all 15 dimensions of so(6), and the 16 at n = 4 generate all 28 of so(8), by explicit repeated bracketing. Adjacency costs DEPTH, not expressiveness.
measurement_3_what_adjacency_costs.control_on_the_closure_instrument: same-qubit generators alone (n of them, no inter-qubit coupling) close on a strictly smaller algebra, so the closure routine can report failure and its positive answers mean something
measurement_3_what_adjacency_costs.the_connection_to_R1B_and_R1C: R1B measured that of the four residuals in the free-fermion certificate exactly one moves under the frame group, and it is `locality`. R1C measured that of the four strategies exactly one is frame-resolving, and it is the one imposing adjacency. This is why: adjacency selects a 5/(2n) slice of so(2n), and WHICH slice depends on the qubit labelling. The residual written in indices is frame-dependent because the structure it refers to genuinely is.

second_correction_this_round.what: the retroactive not-blind control introduced in R1F named three of the four strategies it was written to cover, omitting basis_permutation -- the one whose base value is infinite and which the chosen variants looked least likely to move
second_correction_this_round.outcome: it does move (inf -> 0.0 on a CX ladder, which is basis-confined), so nothing was hidden and no finding changes
second_correction_this_round.why_it_is_recorded_anyway: a control that quietly drops the case least likely to pass is precisely the defect that control exists to detect. The test now covers all four and additionally exercises a deliberately basis-confined circuit rather than relying on one of the variants happening to be one.
second_correction_this_round.bound_correction: self_audit CORRECTIONS entry QSigma-R1h, second of two

where_euler_still_belongs.statement: not at the gate layout -- at the ENCODING. Jordan-Wigner is a one-dimensional fermion-to-qubit encoding and its strings are what make non-adjacent gates non-Gaussian. Encodings whose locality structure is two-dimensional exist in the literature, and under one of those the reachable slice of so(2n) would be determined by a planar mode graph rather than by a line, which is where a Kasteleyn or Euler-characteristic argument would actually apply.
where_euler_still_belongs.status: H. No such encoding is implemented here, none was evaluated, and nothing measured above is evidence about one. This is the corrected location of the idea, not a result about it.

typed_remainders.statement: Everything above is specific to Jordan-Wigner. The reachable fraction 5/(2n), the semantic correctness of adjacency, and the identification of locality as the frame-dependent residual are all statements about that encoding. Under Bravyi-Kitaev or a 2D-local encoding the counting would differ and the adjacency condition would have a different -- possibly larger -- correct form. The instrument does not know which encoding it is in; it is hard-wired to one.

The semantic check ran at n = 3, where gaussian_defect on the full 8x8 unitary is cheap. It scales as O(n 4^n) and the check was not run beyond n = 4. The counting result is exact at all n; the semantic result is measured at small n and argued at large n from the Jordan-Wigner string structure.

The false negative found in measurement 2 is recorded and not repaired. Its size is unknown: no measurement was made of how often circuits in this repository's corpora present a Gaussian operation as a multi-qubit gate. The answer is plausibly zero, and plausibly is not measured.
